newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH KGHM, UNIONS TO MEET ON WAGES MARCH 26.
newsitem.headline: POLISH KGHM, UNIONS TO MEET ON WAGES MARCH 26.

text.p: The board of Poland's KGHM copper concern and trade unions will meet on March 26 on a wage dispute which led to a strike alert last week, the head of the Solidarity union in KGHM said on Tuesday.

Jozef Czyczerski said the seven unions which are in the wage dispute with the management would attend the meeting even though the board was not willing to discuss all postulates, because it came at the time of their regular quarterly meeting.
"This is our regular quarterly meeting with the management so unions will attend, and we shall see what the board will talk about," Czyczerski told Reuter.
The unions demand a 10 percent increase in the basic salary in the company and a 17 percent wage increase for the whole of 1997 against the management's 15 percent.

Sources close to KGHM's board said the management wanted to offer the unions a 17 percent increase in wages throughout 1997, done in two stages -- the first rise on April 1 and the second on July 1, 1997.
"However, the board is not prepared to discuss anything else," the source said.

The unions, fearing lay-offs after KGHM's flotation on Warsaw and London bourses later this year, also wants 10-year employment and social benefit guarantees. KGHM is one of the world's major copper and silver producers.
